entry.summary:
Welcome to Auckland University of Technology’s (AUT) Research Matters! 🚀 AUT’s Research Matters video series is where AUT academics answer everyday questions about their fields of expertise. Get the answer to those questions you’ve always had – or maybe never knew to ask.     

What is play, and why does it matter at every stage of life? How much play do we really need, are we too protective of children, and can online gaming count as genuine play? From Lego and playgrounds to mental health and ageing well, Professor Scott Duncan explores the science and joy of play and why making time for it might be one of the most important things we do. 

00:00 Introduction  
00:18 What is playing?  
00:55 How important is play in our daily lives?  
01:32 How often should we play?  
02:04 Is structured play better for kids or should we let them run wild?  
02:59 Why is Lego so beloved?  
03:40 Are indoor and outdoor play equally good?  
04:20 Are we too protective of kids these days?  
05:21 Should playgrounds be mandatory in new housing developments?  
06:04 What’s your personal favourite type of play?   
06:46 Why is play good for our mental health?  
07:50 Does online gaming count as play?  
08:33 Can you get too old to play?  
08:38 What’s a good sort of play for pensioners?  
09:13 How can we be more playful in our everyday lives?  
10:06 Is how adults play any different to how kids play?  
11:05 I spend a fortune on games, toys, puzzles to encourage my kids to play. Are there free alternatives that are just as good?  
12:14 What does an ideal day look like? 

🔗Check out more on Scott Duncan: https://academics.aut.ac.nz/scott.duncan 

📖Read Scott’s article ‘Play reduces stress and lifts wellbeing’: https://theconversation.com/play-reduces-stress-and-lifts-wellbeing-and-adults-benefit-as-much-as-children-do-264767 

🛝Read Scott’s article ‘Our Changing World: Planning for good days’: https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/ourchangingworld/580572/our-changing-world-planning-for-good-days
